title: Evaluation of Epic® label-free technology to quantify functional recombinant hemagglutinin
author: Jiang, Eichelberger
materials: rHAs of influenza A (H1N1 and H5N1)

To investigate whether the signal could be increased by using fetuin of human origin, the response was measured in wells containing immobilized human recombinant fetuin A (Sigma, St Louis, MO). This recombinant was purified from a mammalian (HEK293 cells) expression system. Due to the expense of this product, a low concentration was immobilized onto the plate. There was good sensitivity in measuring a response of rHA binding to human fetuin (response observed even with 2.5 μg/ml rHA), however the signal was significantly less than the response measured for rHA binding to immobilized bovine fetuin (Figure 4b). Further experiments therefore continued to measure rHA binding to bovine fetuin.

rHAs of influenza A (H1N1 and H5N1) and B viruses were purchased from Protein Science Inc (Meriden, CT) and rHAs of influenza A H7N9 viruses were purchased from Sino Biological (Beijing, China). Bovine and human fetuin, asialofetuin and all other chemicals were purchased from Sigma (St Louis, MO).

steps.title: Gather reagents and plates
steps.instruction: Obtain 384‑well chemically activated Epic plates (Perkin Elmer) and the following reagents: bovine fetuin, asialofetuin (Sigma), rHA preparations (Protein Science or Sino Biological), 20 mM sodium acetate pH 4.5, PBS pH 7.4, 200 mM ethanolamine, 150 mM borate buffer pH 9.2, and a multichannel pipette.

steps.title: Immobilize fetuin on activated plate
steps.instruction: Add 15 µL of ligand solution (150 µg/mL fetuin or asialofetuin in 20 mM sodium acetate, pH 4.5) to each well using a multichannel pipette and incubate at room temperature for 1 hour.

steps.title: Optional ethanolamine blocking
steps.instruction: If desired, block residual reactive groups by adding 200 mM ethanolamine in 150 mM borate buffer (pH 9.2) to each well and incubating for 15 minutes; this step was omitted in the final routine protocol.

steps.title: Wash and add assay buffer
steps.instruction: Wash the plate three times with 25 µL assay buffer (PBS, pH 7.4). After the final wash add 15 µL assay buffer to each well and remove any air bubbles by centrifugation at 400 rpm for 1 minute.

steps.title: Equilibrate and record baseline
steps.instruction: Incubate the plate at room temperature for 4 hours to equilibrate. Record a baseline wavelength reading by comparing the refracted‑light signal from the fetuin‑immobilized sensor to the internal reference sensor in each well.

steps.title: Add rHA dilutions
steps.instruction: Prepare serial dilutions of recombinant HA in dilution buffer (volume 15 µL per well). Add 15 µL of each rHA dilution to quadruplicate wells containing immobilized fetuin (or asialofetuin as negative control).

steps.title: Measure wavelength over time
steps.instruction: Immediately after rHA addition, record the wavelength change 15 times at 2‑minute intervals (total 30 minutes) using the Enspire® multimode plate reader; the instrument reports the difference between the fetuin sensor and the reference sensor in picometers.

steps.title: Analyze data and generate standard curve
steps.instruction: Calculate the response for each well as the difference in wavelength (pm) between fetuin‑immobilized and reference sensors. Plot response versus rHA concentration (2.5–20 µg/mL range) to create a standard curve and determine the concentration of unknown samples from this curve.

steps.title: Determine hemagglutination units
steps.instruction: In a 96‑well round‑bottom plate, serially dilute rHA in PBS. Add 50 µL of 0.5 % turkey red blood cells to each well, mix gently, and let the plate sit at room temperature for 45 minutes. The lowest rHA concentration that produces visible agglutination is recorded as one hemagglutination unit (HAU).
